report:
Summary
- The evidence supports a stylistic/formatting difference, not a clear semantic/domain objective.
- Model B (the B−A residual difference) appears to push the model toward producing short, fragmentary, enumerative/mapping-style continuations (lists, numbered items, “X -> X” identity mappings, small repeated tokens, and compact code-like snippets) when starting a completion.

Why I conclude this
- Localization: the L2-norm of the difference is concentrated overwhelmingly at token position 0 (the first token of the continuation) across many layers, especially middle-to-late layers (layers ~10–25). That indicates the difference primarily affects how the models start their continuations (format/style of the opening tokens).
- Patchscope: injecting the difference produces many outputs that are list-like or transformation-like: enumerations ("1. 22 / 2. 76 ..."), mappings and identity copies ("me -> me", "hello -> hello", "1000 -> 001000"), short newline-separated tokens, simple code lines ("print(\"hello\")"), and repeated small tokens. Multiple layers produce this same family of behavior.
- Logit-lens tokens: the top tokens pointed to by many high-norm cells are short words/heads and tokens commonly used in the starts of lists or short phrases (e.g., numeric/heading tokens, "Stay", "Every", "Best", "Do", and various short nouns/adjectives). The token-level signals are heterogeneous but consistent with a shift in how continuations begin (many tokens useful for short, fragmentary starts).

What I do not claim
- There is no clear, specific semantic domain (e.g., politics, medical advice) that the evidence supports naming. The logit-lens token set is mixed (some mentions of "tragic", "law", "surgeon", etc.), but patchscope consistently shows a change in output shape/format rather than a stable topical preference. So the safest, supported interpretation is a style/format bias rather than a content objective.

Short conclusion
- The difference is a change in generation style: Model B is biased toward starting continuations with short, enumerative/transformational, and repetitive/list-like outputs compared to Model A. The evidence does not support naming a more specific semantic objective.
